**Short answer:** *Take the contract only if you can guarantee that the capitation rate, risk‑adjustment, stop‑loss, and quality‑bonus structure will cover your true cost of care (including high‑cost patients) and protect physicians from underpayment penalties. In most cases a 40‑physician group with a 25 000‑member panel would need to negotiate significant concessions before the deal is defensible.* Below is a step‑by‑step framework that shows how you can evaluate the offer, what the “defensible” deal should look like, and where the key risks lie. --- ## 1. Financial Viability | Item | What to calculate | Typical Medicare Advantage benchmark | |------|-------------------|-------------------------------------| | **Gross capitation** | $1,180 PMPM × 25 000 = **$354 million/yr** | 10–15 % lower than FFS for similar panels | | **Risk‑adjusted rate** | Must be indexed to the panel’s HCC score (or CMS risk score). | A 5 % higher rate per 1‑point increase in HCC is common. | | **Average cost per member per month (ACPM)** | Sum of: primary care visits, specialty referrals, hospitalizations, pharmacy, home health, etc., divided by 25 000. | Medicare Advantage panels typically spend $1,000–$1,200 CPM; high‑risk panels can exceed $1,400 CPM. | | **Stop‑loss / risk corridor** | A ceiling on the amount you pay for a member (e.g., 10 % of total capitation or $X per episode). | Many contracts include a “stop‑loss” that caps losses above a threshold; otherwise you bear all high‑cost risk. | | **Quality bonus pool** | HEDIS thresholds + any CMS quality bonuses (often $50–$150 k/yr for a 25 000 panel). | Bonuses are usually <5 % of total capitation but can be higher if the payer is aggressive on quality. | | **Penalty exposure** | Under‑performance penalties (e.g., 1–3 % of capitation per metric shortfall). | Penalties can erode 2–4 % of revenue if you miss a few metrics. | ### Bottom line - **If your projected ACPM is ≤ $1,180 CPM** and the risk‑adjusted rate covers that, the deal is *financially neutral* at best. - **If your ACPM > $1,180 CPM**, you need either a higher capitation or generous stop‑loss coverage to avoid losses. --- ## 2. Clinical Operations Readiness | Risk | Mitigation in Deal | |------|--------------------| | **Care coordination overload** | Contract must include reimbursement for care managers (e.g., $30–$50 k/yr per manager) and/or a carve‑out for high‑risk patients. | | **Provider burnout / low visit volume** | Include a “visit bonus” or “volume floor” that guarantees a minimum number of reimbursed visits per physician, or allow physicians to bill FFS for certain services (e.g., complex procedures). | | **Quality data collection & reporting** | Require the payer to provide real‑time dashboards and audit rights. Specify that all HEDIS measures must be tracked in your EHR with automated alerts. | | **Telehealth & preventive care** | Negotiate a higher rate for telemedicine visits (e.g., 20 % above standard) and a separate incentive for meeting preventive screening targets. | ### Key operational clauses 1. **Care‑management carve‑out** – A fixed fee per high‑risk member that covers case management, medication reconciliation, and home health coordination. 2. **Visit‑volume guarantee** – Minimum reimbursed visits per physician (e.g., 200/yr) with a penalty if below. 3. **Data sharing & audit rights** – Payer must provide access to all claims data within 30 days; you have the right to audit for compliance and quality. --- ## 3. Legal Exposure | Issue | How to protect yourself | |-------|------------------------| | **Anti‑kickback / self‑referral statutes** | Ensure that any “bonus” or “carve‑out” is tied strictly to objective performance metrics, not to specific referrals. | | **HIPAA & data privacy** | Include a robust Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with the payer; specify encryption and breach notification timelines. | | **CMS contract compliance** | The contract must be vetted by an attorney experienced in Medicare Advantage contracts; include a clause that allows you to terminate if CMS changes regulations that materially affect your payment model. | | **Indemnification** | Payer should indemnify the group for any claims arising from payer‑initiated audits or regulatory actions, provided the group has complied with all contractual obligations. | --- ## 4. Sample Deal Structure (Defensible) | Component | Suggested Terms | |-----------|-----------------| | **Base capitation** | $1,180 PMPM + risk adjustment: +$10 CPM per HCC point above panel average. | | **Stop‑loss** | Cap losses at 10 % of total capitation; payer pays any episode >$30 k. | | **Quality bonuses** | • HEDIS ≥90 % → $100 k bonus
• CMS quality score ≥95 % → $150 k bonus
• Penalties: −2 % per metric shortfall | | **Care‑management carve‑out** | $35 k/yr per high‑risk member (HCC > 3) for case management, medication reconciliation, and home health coordination. | | **Visit volume guarantee** | Minimum of 200 reimbursed visits per physician; if below, payer pays a flat $5 k per shortfall visit. | | **Telehealth incentive** | 20 % higher rate for telemedicine visits; separate bonus for ≥80 % of visits conducted via telehealth. | | **Governance & audit** | Joint oversight committee (payer + group), quarterly performance reviews, and right to audit all claims within 30 days. | | **Legal safeguards** | BAA, indemnification clause, anti‑kickback compliance language, termination rights for regulatory changes. | --- ## 5. Recommendation 1. **If you have a mature care‑management infrastructure (case managers, robust EMR reporting, proven quality metrics)** and can demonstrate that your ACPM is ≤ $1,180 CPM after risk adjustment, the contract *could* be acceptable—provided you negotiate the stop‑loss, carve‑outs, and visit guarantees above. 2. **If you lack those capabilities** (e.g., limited case management, low quality scores, high proportion of high‑risk patients), the risk of underpayment is too great. In that scenario: - Decline the offer *or* - Negotiate a higher base rate (e.g., $1,300 PMPM) and/or a more generous stop‑loss (e.g., 15 % of capitation). - Consider a hybrid model where you retain FFS for high‑cost services. 3. **Always have the contract reviewed by an attorney** with Medicare Advantage experience before signing. The devil is in the details—especially around quality metrics, data sharing, and indemnification clauses. --- ### Bottom line *Take it only if you can guarantee that the capitation rate plus risk adjustment will cover your true cost of care, and you have built-in safeguards (stop‑loss, carve‑outs, visit guarantees) that protect against underpayment. Otherwise, negotiate aggressively or walk away.*
